1	# Request and criteria handoff
2	
3	Use for delegated asset work when a proposed production contract is ready to adopt, or when its consequential request/criteria change. The specialist prepares the contract; the calling agent independently compares its actual contents to the original assignment. This is an agent-to-agent review, not a new user-approval gate. Continue under established authorization when the contract is consistent.
4	
5	## Specialist: return the exact proposed contract
6	
7	Use the focused authoring context described in [family delivery](family-delivery.md)
8	to locate current records before exploring histories. Keep a proposal's shared
9	source index once and reference its entries from individual clauses; preserve each
10	clause's authority, scope and exact locator. Do not duplicate whole reports in
11	every criterion, abbreviate literal checks into a group summary, or treat the
12	index's source class as requirement authority. Read the original source text for
13	the comparison; retrieve a complete record/history only where it bears on the
14	decision. Exact connected review remains the handoff for adoption.
15	
16	For a connected family/stage plan, use the adapter's returned `request_review`
17	arguments and retain that exact report as described in
18	[the connected handoff](#connected-family-and-stage-handoff). It supplies the saved
19	criteria and request evidence without manually rebuilding a candidate packet.
20	
21	For other contracts, save a compact `request-review.json` in the consumer project. Point to existing artifacts instead of duplicating provider history or manufacturing PX2 state for a planning-only task. Its fields are:
22	
23	- `version`: 1.
24	- `sources`: the brief and relevant consumer/reference sources, each with project-relative `path`, actual byte `sha256`, and `role`; include locators for the adopted decisions. Numbered locators refer to that individual file, never a concatenated multi-file terminal display. The caller verifies the cited content at those locators. Include the selected `requirements_hash` when PLAR supplied one.
25	- `request`: `path`, `sha256`, `kind` (`provider_arguments` or `creative_brief`) and the actual tool name when known. Provider arguments must be the complete exact JSON to dispatch, including real reference inputs. Use a creative brief when an operation/schema has not been discovered; do not label it executable.
26	- `criteria`: `path` and `sha256` for the exact criteria to use. Each criterion has an ID, check, authority/basis, applicable scope and source locator. Distinguish owner/consumer requirements, specialist sample choices, observations and diagnostics.
27	- `choices`: the consequential specialist choices or unresolved decisions, where each appears in the request/criteria, and its reason. A criterion scoped to a chosen sample can assess that sample; it does not establish a universal project requirement.
28	- `resume`: existing store/task/output/job links when applicable. Omit absent production state.
29	
30	Return the packet's path and SHA-256 to the caller. For PX2 production, link the saved request and Q records or an exact exported view with their state/record identity. Do not silently rebuild the request after review. Before dispatch, compare the actual arguments to the reviewed request; reference bytes/handles and non-text controls matter as much as prompt wording.
31	
32	Keep a required outcome separate from the recipe proposed to achieve it. A qualitative requirement such as matching a reference or conveying a state still needs an acceptance criterion when its palette, geometry, frame count or layout are open. When demoting an unsupported recipe to a sample choice, preserve the underlying required outcome; do not leave only mechanical checks binding. Consumer code establishes its actual data/rendering behavior, not an unmeasured aesthetic quality. Attribute expert quality criteria to expert judgment where that is their basis.
33	
34	Creative decisions within the assignment need not all go back to the user. For example, choosing a static first sample or a construction method is expert judgment; attributing it to an owner who specified only canvas dimensions is incorrect. Keep the choice explicit and scoped so it can be revised without changing the owner's brief. Observations alone do not become rejection rules.
35	
36	### Measured facts in creative requests
37	
38	Do not estimate pixel coordinates by eye and then describe them as verified. When a numerical image fact materially guides a request or verdict, retain the measurement with its source-image hash, frame and coordinate convention. The existing `asset-check --regions COLOR...` / `pixl_asset_check(regions=[...])` measures exact RGBA component boxes; it does not identify the subject or make those colors mandatory. Boxes use zero-based coordinates with exclusive right/bottom edges. For other measurements, save the reproducible calculation. When exact coordinates are unnecessary, describe the visual relationship and supply the actual reference instead.
39	
40	Keep centering calculations in one coordinate convention. For a half-open box
41	`[left, top, right, bottom]`, its centre in pixel-edge coordinates is
42	`((left + right) / 2, (top + bottom) / 2)` and the canvas centre is `(width / 2, height / 2)`.
43	A centroid computed from zero-based pixel indices needs `+0.5` per axis to use those
44	same edge coordinates. A margin imbalance, box-centre offset and mass-centroid offset
45	are different quantities; retain the actual calculation before calling an asset centred.
46	
47	The caller independently verifies consequential measured claims against the original image and measurement, including the coordinate convention; repeating a specialist's pixel map is not independent verification. Correct unsupported numbers before dispatch while preserving the required visual outcome.
48	
49	## Resolve source evidence for the comparison
50	
51	For candidate plans used by selected-asset preparation, call `pixl_request_review`
52	with the packet path and selected `asset_id` (CLI `request-review PACKET --asset ID
53	--root PROJECT`). It reads the exact request/criteria identities, returns cited text
54	with file-local bounds, and includes the current production continuation. It reports
55	invalid/unresolved locators and changed sources. A resolved excerpt is evidence for
56	the caller to interpret, not a consistency verdict. Retain this report with the review.
57	
58	Copy a host-spilled tool report as exact bytes before inspecting or formatting it.
59	These tool reports are UTF-8 JSON: use an explicit UTF-8 decoder (for example,
60	`Path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")`), not the Windows process default. If saving a
61	formatted copy, compare its parsed value with the raw report before returning its
62	path/hash. A new file hash alone cannot detect text changed by a wrong decoder.
63	Keep the raw report alongside any formatted copy.
64	
65	When the connection is already discovered, bind `request.provider` and
66	`request.connection: {path, sha256}` to its exact artifact. Preparation compares that
67	reviewed connection with the supplied one; host credentials stay outside the artifact.
68	
69	Use `lines: [first,last]` on a criterion's source pointer when citing text; retain
70	`locator` as a human-readable label. Preparation validates explicit bounds before
71	saving new work. Numbered prose in older plans remains readable and receives
72	locator diagnostics. For non-text references inspect the actual image/animation;
73	for named sections resolve the location through the existing source tool. Do not
74	mark a locator verified merely because its claimed wording appears elsewhere.
75	
76	The optional criterion `authority` uses PLAR's requirement/proposal/observation/unknown
77	labels. Keep its basis and scope explicit. This label is an assertion to compare,
78	not an automatic grant of owner authority.
79	
80	## Caller: inspect before adopting
81	
82	### Connected family and stage handoff
83	
84	`pixl_production_plan` and `pixl_stage_prepare` return `request_review` arguments
85	for this same review tool. Pass that object to `pixl_request_review`; `packet`
86	names the store's `state.px`, `plan` names its exact connected-plan X, and `job`
87	is present after preparation. Existing plans can use those IDs directly. The
88	report includes every authored member and collective criterion with its full Q
89	ID, record hash, literal check and source evidence. Authority starts unclassified:
90	source presence or a validator pass cannot assign it. Changed plan/source/PLAR
91	identities remain visible so historical interpretation can be reviewed without
92	making an obsolete request current.
93	
94	The specialist returns this report's path/hash, explicit choices and any proposed
95	corrections. The caller reads the original evidence and records one
96	`criterion_comparisons` entry for **each** returned ID, including collective rules:
97	
98	```json
99	{
100	  "review_scope_sha256": "REPORT_REVIEW_SCOPE_HASH",
101	  "criterion_comparisons": [{
102	    "criterion": "EXACT_Q_ID",
103	    "record_sha256": "Q_RECORD_HASH",
104	    "source_obligation": "What the cited source actually requires, with locator",
105	    "authority_basis": "Required outcome, scoped expert choice, observation, or mixed clauses",
106	    "scope": "The asset, stage or chosen construction this rule applies to",
107	    "literal_delta": "What the exact rule adds, drops or leaves unchanged",
108	    "discriminating_alternative": "A concrete alternative that tests that difference",
109	    "disposition": "Keep, clarify or correct, with the proposed artifact identity"
110	  }]
111	}
112	```
113	
114	Split mixed-authority clauses in these explanations. A sound construction does
115	not make every clause an owner requirement; nor does an expert choice need to be
116	removed merely because other valid methods exist. Keep the required artistic
117	outcome and identify the chosen method's narrower scope. Do not substitute one
118	grouped style/geometry assertion for this comparison.
119	
120	Call the same tool with `comparison` pointing to the saved caller file to check
121	coverage and identity. Missing, repeated, stale or incomplete rows are reported.
122	`complete:true` means structural coverage only; semantic judgment remains the
123	caller’s responsibility, and `consistent` stays null in the tool report. Record
124	the caller's own disposition separately. Save a corrected proposal beside the
125	old plan/request when necessary; do not rewrite historical criteria, transplant
126	acceptance or prepare another job merely to repair the review.
127	
128	### Compare the original sources and exact contract
129	
130	For either route, open the retained packet/report and verify its hashes. Read the original brief, relevant sources, complete request and complete criteria, not just the specialist's summary or self-audit. Check:
131	
132	1. Every explicit requirement survives into the request and relevant checks, including qualitative identity/style/state outcomes, actual reference role/input and consumer mapping. Check for dropped or weakened outcomes as well as added restrictions.
133	2. Every consequential extra restriction has its true basis and scope. Test whether a brief-conforming alternative would be rejected only because an observation or proposal was promoted to an owner requirement.
134	3. The proposed operation's actual declaration supports the payload. Do not infer a provider parameter, frame/direction count, alpha policy or camera from prose alone.
135	4. Findings concern these exact artifacts. Mechanical/hash validity and a specialist's consistency claim do not prove semantic agreement or artistic quality.
136	5. Each rejection rule belongs to the current candidate/stage and has satisfiable prerequisites. A first sample cannot require completed dependent family assets before it may be accepted. Retain deferred family or destination obligations with an explicit later stage in the handoff/PLAR; verify they remain scheduled rather than dropping the required outcome.
137	
138	For each rejection criterion, save one concise comparison using the following
139	sequence. A table or JSON is sufficient; this is the caller's actual reasoning about
140	the source, not a worksheet to have the specialist certify for itself.
141	
142	1. **Source obligation.** Derive the minimum required outcome from the original source
143	   wording and locator before using the draft criterion as its paraphrase. State what
144	   the source leaves open. For an expert criterion, identify the actual expert choice
145	   and candidate scope instead of inventing owner authority.
146	2. **Literal condition and additions.** Compare the entire check with that obligation.
147	   Identify the exact added or omitted words/clauses, including extent, composition,
148	   exclusions, comparisons and numerical bounds. A supported noun does not establish
149	   support for its modifiers. Read the check itself, not just its basis or label.
150	3. **Discriminating alternative.** For each added restriction, describe a plausible
151	   asset that keeps the source obligation true while making that specific restriction
152	   false. Name the clause being tested and whether the literal check would reject it.
153	   Merely changing a value the check already permits does not test that restriction.
154	   If the source itself excludes the alternative, identify the exact source support.
155	4. **Disposition.** Keep the required outcome; remove an unsupported narrowing from
156	   that rule or split it into an explicitly scoped expert choice with its own rationale.
157	   An ambiguous condition that could reject a valid alternative needs clearer wording;
158	   do not approve it by silently giving it a more permissive interpretation. Verify the
159	   correction in the returned artifact before marking the contract consistent.
160	
161	For example, a requirement for a readable silhouette does not itself require an
162	outlined silhouette. Comparing two outline colours leaves the added outline rule
163	untested; a readable outline-free construction tests it. The specialist may still
164	recommend an outline for this sample and explain its artistic value. The comparison
165	preserves that expertise while accurately describing who chose it and what it binds.
166	
167	Cover every rejection rule; group only genuinely identical ones. Retain the source
168	quote/bounds, literal delta, tested alternative and disposition together. A general
169	"the brief permits flexibility" statement or a prompt-choice label elsewhere cannot
170	cancel a restriction still present in an owner-authority acceptance condition.
171	
172	Check the **review route** as well as the wording. A local mechanical check can
173	establish measured dimensions, frame counts or alpha values. It cannot decide which
174	shape is intentional foreground, whether a matte is unwanted, whether a silhouette
175	reads as the requested symbol, or whether an accent serves its role. For a mixed
176	criterion, either split the measurement and required visual judgment or set its mode
177	to `visual` (normally domain `visual` too). The runtime requires saved native/enlarged
178	candidate views for visual-mode or visual/continuity-domain reviews; labelling such a
179	condition `mechanical`/`local` bypasses that evidence requirement. A planning-only
180	correction must still specify the route its future acceptance will actually need.
181	Do not call a corrected contract operable merely because its source locators resolve.
182	
183	When reviewing a specialist's response to a discrepancy, re-open the literal check.
184	An added attribution or a claim that a conventional construction excludes no valid
185	alternatives does not remove an unchanged mandatory recipe. Retain the source's
186	qualitative outcome as required and place the expert construction in a scoped proposal;
187	judge actual recognizability without declaring one geometric recipe universal.
188	
189	Resolve every evidence-report diagnostic before calling a locator verified. For a
190	text citation, open the actual source, use its file-local inclusive bounds and save
191	those bounds in the corrected packet; a nearby matching sentence does not repair a
192	wrong range. An unresolved named or visual reference needs actual inspection and a
193	recorded finding. A source hash alone never verifies the cited location or its meaning.
194	
195	The [delegation boundary](delegation.md#caller--specialist) distinguishes unchanged
196	historical evidence from the editable corrected proposal. A caller must not freeze
197	prior criterion text or authority in the new proposal; reassess those interpretations
198	against the source. Use the profile's visual-role distinctions when translating colour,
199	subject construction and transparency intent, rather than adding a construction rule.
200	
201	If a contract defect is found after delivery, preserve the original request, plan,
202	verdicts and candidate. Save a corrected proposal and independent comparison as a new
203	artifact, explicitly distinguishing it from the historical contract used for delivery.
204	Do not create another provider job merely to correct documentation, transplant old
205	verdicts to new criteria, or silently rewrite durable completed work. Carry both the
206	historical identity and the correction's adoption scope in the exact handoff details.
207	
208	Keep process requirements, output requirements and diagnostic proxies distinct. A required production route is checked through actual calls and downloaded-byte provenance; a property of the resulting image is evidence only when it establishes that claim. Do not silently turn a process restriction into an extra output-difference test, or a diagnostic into a rejection rule. Independent review uses the original source, not another agent's assertion that the rule is sourced.
209	
210	Save a concise `caller-review.json` (or equivalent named fields) with reviewer role, reviewed packet hash, `consistent` / `changes_requested` / `needs_input`, per-criterion comparisons and other findings tied to request locations and source evidence, and the next action. `consistent` means the planned contract matches this assignment; it is not provider execution or asset acceptance.
211	
212	If changes are needed, send the specialist the precise discrepancy and relevant source; preserve the original artifacts, revise only the affected contract, and inspect the returned new packet. Reuse the existing specialist when the host supports it. Resolve supplied facts yourself; ask the user only a consequential decision genuinely missing from the available context. No token, secret header or credential belongs in either file.
213	
214	If no independent caller/reviewer exists, retain the specialist's own review as self-review, proceed within existing authorization, and report the independent comparison as unperformed. Do not invent another agent or stop ordinary direct work solely to satisfy this procedure.
215	
216	## Carry the comparison through production
217	
218	Return `request_review` in the normal result, containing the packet and caller-review paths/hashes and unresolved findings. After preparing the durable provider job, verify its actual request still matches the reviewed arguments. A changed requirement, criterion or request needs a new comparison; polling progress and unrelated queue changes do not.
219	
220	The final caller opens the delivered assets, checks the actual request and output against this contract, and records its own observations. Keep contract consistency, provider outcome, visual quality and destination acceptance separate. For a rejected candidate, retain the failure and the revised request/criteria; changing a checker merely to pass the candidate is a contract change, not an asset correction.
221	
222	When an artistic explanation asserts a measurement, compare that assertion with
223	its actual data and coordinate convention. Reproducing a bounding box does not
224	verify a stated axis angle or arm-length ratio; approximate visual descriptions
225	should remain approximate. Correct an inconsistent explanation in a new observation
226	without converting its sample geometry into an additional rejection condition.
227	Reassess the original claim using its stated inputs. For quoted endpoints, retain
228	the coordinate convention and calculate their deltas, lengths and angles before
229	confirming an axis or ratio. Counts of occupied pixels, a bounding box and a newly
230	estimated centreline measure different things; they cannot confirm the original
231	endpoint claim. Save the old claim, calculation and corrected interpretation together
232	so the caller can reproduce the comparison without inheriting the earlier assertion.
233	
234	## Start a successor comparison with the concise view
235	
236	For two retained connected plans, call `pixl_request_review` with `view:"changes"`,
237	`plan` and explicit `against_plan`; CLI: `request-review STATE --plan NEW --against-plan OLD --view changes --root ROOT`.
238	Save with `result_path` / `--result-path`. Use the change counts, retained choices,
239	source drift and review attention to choose what to inspect. Then follow both
240	full-report retrievals and compare the exact literal criteria. The compact view
241	does not declare semantic equivalence, direct succession, consistency or approval.
242	All old/new IDs/hashes remain indexed; renamed clauses require explicit mapping.
243	
244	Focused `pixl_context(view:"authoring")` expands explicitly linked choices and
245	their authority dependencies. Inspect `choice_scope.other_intake` when an unlinked
246	caller choice may apply; its retrieval links preserve access to the full record.
247	Do not promote observed/proposed values to confirmed requirements or infer that
248	an omitted full value is irrelevant. Keep the independent caller's interpretation
249	separate from the tool's deterministic structural comparison.

1	# Intake through a reviewed representative sample
2	
3	Use this operation for an incomplete brief, a consequential artistic uncertainty, or the first representative item/pose/cycle/neighborhood before producing a family. Follow the [production profile](../../../resources/agent/PROFILE.md). This reference governs PIXL operation; maintaining this repository remains a development task.
4	
5	## Required context and entry
6	
7	Read the actual [PX2 specification](../../../resources/spec/PIXL-2.md) and [registry](../../../runtime/pixl/registry-v2.json). New lifecycle projects use `intake STORE --name NAME --brief TEXT --root PROJECT_ROOT`, or `pixl_intake`. It creates a project and actors without a style contract. Existing PX1 state keeps its version; `workflow` deliberately rejects it. Do not relabel an old header, invent past confirmation, or discard old evidence to migrate it.
8	
9	Inspect available references and artifacts at native scale and enlarged scale. Identify which choices affect this operation and which can remain unresolved. Preserve the user's actual instruction or relevant observation in project-owned source files, then record S identities/ranges. The profile supplies the judgment; dimensions, binary alpha and fixed palettes are not universal requirements.
10	
11	## Keep authority through derived rules
12	
13	Before deriving a style contract, acceptance criterion, checker rule or provider instruction, retain a compact account of each consequential restriction: property/value, authority and status, exact supporting instruction or adopted project choice, and where the restriction applies. Use the existing choice/source fields in PIXL state; this account adds no UDL fields. Carry its status through the entire approach, including prompts, checks and handoff.
14	
15	The user's instruction and adopted project choices establish requirements. Reference pixels establish observations; matching a reference does not adopt every measured dimension, color, gap, alpha level or component count as a mandatory rule. For an unspecified property, explain a project-specific proposal and the trial it would test. A proposed trial can proceed within existing authorization while the final production choice remains open.
16	
17	A supplied palette expressed as color roles or families preserves those choices without automatically making sampled reference hex values an exclusive allowed-color list. Use exact working colors as a scoped proposal when useful; attribute exact restrictions to the owner only when their instruction or adoption establishes them. Binary transparency constrains alpha, while opaque edge colors and anti-aliasing require their own authority. Keep these distinctions in the saved contract and criteria, and continue the authorized sample work without asking the caller to repeat settled choices.
18	
19	If your interpretation of an image differs from the brief's terminology, describe the observed pixels and the uncertainty while preserving the requested treatment. An alternative that contradicts that treatment is a change for the user to adopt, not a correction you can silently install in the contract. Neither a tool default nor a passing checker supplies that adoption.
20	
21	Keep diagnostic conclusions attached to their tested artifact, method, scale and background. Failure of one resized fixture does not establish a minimum canvas for other designs; a measured component count or contrast ratio does not establish a universal rejection threshold. Label verified tool limitations separately from artistic choices.
22	
23	Before saving the approach or a verdict, trace every enforced artistic restriction back to that account. Correct downstream claims such as “approved,” “binding,” or “must” when their source is still observed, proposed or unresolved. Preserve the earlier draft and its evidence when correcting it.
24	
25	For a selected PLAR asset's first concrete candidate, use [PLAR preparation](../../plar/references/prepare.md) to save the reviewed output/criteria plan and first durable request in one operation. The record-level sequence below remains available for advanced plans and explicit amendments.
26	
27	## Preserve intake and plan before execution
28	
29	1. Load the current state and canonical hash. Decode it through the runner, keeping `format: 2` in the host adapter. Amend the relevant fields, increase the revision by one, encode a candidate, validate against the project root, and commit with the previously observed hash. A stale-write error means reload and reconcile.
30	2. Add each consequential choice as I with project, actor, key, status, value, sources and rationale; add it to P.in. Unknown values are null. Observations, proposals and confirmations remain different statuses. Preserve conflicting alternatives instead of selecting a scaffold default.
31	3. Research the uncertain technique through the [knowledge operation](knowledge.md). A K recipe or reference POC is useful context, not a proof for this asset. 1	# PixelLab operation and reference selection
2	
3	Start with the [official documentation](https://www.pixellab.ai/docs) and [complete MCP tool guide](https://api.pixellab.ai/mcp/docs). Discover the actual connected tool declaration for the selected operation. Documentation across the web/editor/MCP/REST surfaces can describe different input limits and output packaging. Match the surface, not just the marketing name.
4	
5	Prefer the connected official PixelLab MCP tools for agent production. Use the existing HTTP adapter when that explicitly selected route supports the task; its single image endpoint does not represent the full platform. A missing MCP tool does not justify guessing a REST endpoint or silently choosing a weaker operation.
6	
7	## Choose by the deliverable
8	
9	For dependent operations, such as an accepted seed followed by animation or an
10	edit, use [connected stage authoring](../../../resources/spec/production-plan.md)
11	to retain the prerequisite output and bind its exact selected candidate before
12	preparing the next request. This local adapter preserves the reviewed inputs;
13	the host still supplies actual image handles and executes the official tool.
14	
15	The names below are discovery starting points, not a frozen callable catalog.
16	
17	| Need | Discover and evaluate |
18	| --- | --- |
19	| Small standalone sprite, item or UI icon | Freeform image tools, including Pixen, Pixflux and Pro/Pro Flash; compare exact canvas, image conditioning and output count |
20	| UI panel, frame or component set | UI asset tools; examine pieces/states, border geometry and current canvas limits |
21	| Pixel font | Font creation and retrieval; verify required glyphs, atlas/TTF delivery and actual text rendering |
22	| Character identity across directions | Character tools, existing-character state operations and supplied direction support |
23	| Object/environment prop across directions | Object tools and object-state variants |
24	| Motion | Character/object animation for an existing resource, or image animation for loose sprites; preserve timing, anchors and frame/direction expectations |
25	| Terrain | The matching top-down, sidescroller, isometric or tile tool; reuse connected base tiles and validate adjacency |
26	| Repair or variation | Edit/inpaint or state operations on the existing source; identify exactly what must remain unchanged |
27	| Material response or authored effects | Normal-map and pixel/VFX workbench tools when the assignment needs those outputs |
28	
29	Do not choose a tool merely because “UI” or “character” appears in the task. For example, an icon's native canvas can be smaller than a UI panel operation accepts. Generate at the appropriate native scale or explain a proposed adaptation; resizing an oversized result is not automatically equivalent pixel art.
30	
31	Inspect output cardinality before submission: a candidate grid, eight directions and one image are different deliverables. Do not order additional variants just because a mode returns them. Query capability/quote tools where available; preserve their provisional meaning and the user's current limits. No cached price or old tool inventory establishes the current charge or entitlement.
32	
33	## Preserve reference meaning in actual arguments
34	
35	Assign each visual input a role before selecting the operation:
36	
37	| Role | Preserve |
38	| --- | --- |
39	| style | Art language: selected palette/ramp behavior, outlines, shading, detail and cluster scale |
40	| identity | The particular subject, costume, silhouette or already approved sprite |
41	| pose | Orientation, gesture, contact and anatomical placement |
42	| layout | Spatial arrangement, UI pieces, safe areas or composition |
43	| palette | Explicit color choices when adopted, rather than incidental reference measurements |
44	| mask | The actual region to change/preserve with the selected tool's mask semantics |
45	| motion | Timing/pose sequence or motion reference |
46	
47	PLAR's optional `references` entries record `source`, `role` and `instructions`. Sources bind actual project files; selected context carries their current identities. A source citation or a filename written in a text prompt does **not** transmit an image to PixelLab.
48	
49	Inspect the chosen tool's image inputs. For an image on disk, discover `get_upload_url` first when the operation accepts an image URL. Follow its returned upload instructions to send the file bytes directly (for example, multipart `curl -F file=@PATH`; `curl.exe` on Windows), parse the actual response, and use its returned `upload:<id>` in the corresponding image URL field. Bind that handle to the original local hash and role in the reviewed request. Keep the temporary upload URL out of delivery artifacts. This avoids model transcription of encoded image data; manually pasted base64 can corrupt even a small PNG.
50	
51	Transfer the actual image via its supported upload URL/handle, owned source ID, URL or encoded payload. Use `get_upload_url` and its returned instructions for local images when available; prefer supported handles/URLs to large inline base64. Keep the local source hash, its role, the returned handle and the exact request field associated in production evidence. Upload handles are temporary transport references, not durable replacements for local source files.
52	
53	Use the role-specific input: a style anchor is not necessarily a subject/pose source, and an init image can influence composition as well as appearance. Reusing an approved character or object ID can preserve identity more directly than describing it again. For Pro Flash, inspect current native sizes and style-image fit; the style anchor and content-reference count are distinct concepts. Reuse the chosen family anchor and relevant controls across members, then inspect the actual results.
54	
55	If the chosen operation cannot express a required reference role, select a supported operation or propose a concrete staged workflow. A text-only fallback needs to be identified as an approximation; do not present it as equivalent reference conditioning. Avoid adding an unrelated exact-palette restriction merely because a style image has a small measured color set.
56	
57	The [style-reference workflow](https://www.pixellab.ai/docs/tools/consistent-style) explains style consistency, while [init-image options](https://www.pixellab.ai/docs/options/init-image) explain image-guided generation. Their editor controls do not substitute for the live MCP input schema. The [UI workflow](https://www.pixellab.ai/docs/tools/create-ui-elements-pro) informs design intent; verify the actual MCP UI operation's limits independently.
58	
59	## Run and review
60	
61	Use [provider recovery](provider-recovery.md) for saved intent and actual calls. Capture returned IDs, use the matching retrieval tool, and use bounded `wait_for_jobs` when appropriate instead of blind repeated polling. Retrieve actual output files before inspection.
62	
63	Review the asset's intended function at its display size: state readability for UI, identity and volume across directions, timing and contact in playback, adjacency in terrain, and alpha/material behavior in the target renderer. Keep source art and failed candidates. Prefer a targeted edit of a nearly correct result when it preserves the required identity; do not erase the original.
64	
65	For animation, distinguish requested generated frames from the tool's returned
66	sequence: some operations include the supplied input frame in addition to generated
67	frames. Retain every returned frame, declare any selection/assembly explicitly,
68	and check the consumer's exact frame count and last-to-first transition. A provider
69	claim of transparency is not a per-frame alpha check. Inspect each actual frame for
70	matte leaks, shape drift and unintended holds before acceptance.
71	
72	Use the host's pixel-art judgment and the official platform's deterministic editing
73	tools when they better preserve a useful generated result. Retain the source,
74	guard edits against observed pixels and verify what changed. Distinguish a generated
75	pose with specialist-constructed motion from motion produced by an animation model;
76	both can serve the asset, but their provenance and quality evidence differ. A failed
77	background-removal attempt can leave a useful opaque retry requiring an explicitly
78	reviewed cutout. Preserve the failed attempt and review the corrected candidate anew.
79	
80	Return the [caller result](delegation.md) with files, checks, remaining questions and real provider/state identifiers. The platform creates candidates; the specialist supplies design judgment and evidence of fit.
81

1	# Outline and canvas decision brief
2	
3	This is both the decision brief for the project owner and the retained visual
4	observation backing criterion `q_aid_useful` for candidate `x_aid`.
5	
6	- **Sheet:** `deliverables/outline-scale-comparison.png`
7	- **Built from:** the supplied `reference.png` and `reference-b.png` bytes only, enlarged
8	  by integer nearest-neighbour at 1x, 2x, 3x, 4x, 6x and 8x over light, dark and busy
9	  backgrounds. No content was redrawn or resampled; the accompanying local check
10	  (`evidence/aid-faithfulness.json`) confirmed all 36 panels and 14,040 opaque source
11	  pixels enlarge into uniform blocks with no invented colour.
12	- **Reviewer:** PIXL (agent), viewed in this session, 2026-09-14.
13	- **Outcome for `q_aid_useful`:** pass, with one stated limit.
14	
15	## What the sheet shows
16	
17	**The outline decision is really a background decision.** This is the finding that
18	matters, and it is not visible in either reference on its own.
19	
20	- On the **light** band both treatments read well. The unoutlined teal has ample
21	  contrast against a pale field and needs no help; the outline adds articulation but is
22	  not doing separation work.
23	- On the **dark** band the navy outline is close enough in value to the background that
24	  it partly disappears. The outlined figure reads as a *smaller* teal shape with a soft
25	  dark fringe, and the top stalks nearly vanish because they are entirely outline
26	  colour. The unoutlined figure reads more strongly and holds its full size.
27	- On the **busy** band the relationship inverts. The dark contour is what lifts the
28	  outlined figure off the noisy mid-value field, while the unoutlined teal begins to
29	  blend into it, particularly at the smaller scales.
30	
31	So: if the game's levels are predominantly dark, the outline in `reference.png` actively
32	costs readability. If the levels are busy or mid-value, the outline is what makes the
33	character separable. Choosing the outline without knowing the backgrounds risks picking
34	the treatment that fails where the game actually is.
35	
36	**The outline costs apparent size.** At 6x and 8x the teal interior of the outlined
37	figure is visibly smaller than the full teal body of the unoutlined one. The 2 px
38	contour consumes 180 of 390 visible pixels. On a canvas smaller than the references'
39	32 x 32, that cost grows proportionally and leaves very little interior in which a scout
40	and a medic could differ from one another.
41	
42	**Legibility of the difference by scale.** At 1x the two treatments are not reliably
43	distinguishable — the figure is 18 x 25 device pixels and the outline reads as a general
44	darkening rather than as a contour. At 2x the eyes resolve. From 3x upward the outline
45	treatment is unambiguous. This is the stated limit on the pass: the sheet supports the
46	decision at 3x and above, and shows that at 1x the decision barely matters visually.
47	
48	## What this does not decide
49	
50	The sheet does not choose for you. Per the bundled `edge-rhythm` method, contour style is
51	authored intent and must not be resolved mechanically, and per `silhouette-readability`,
52	no contrast ratio or pixel count proves aesthetic quality. Both treatments are viable;
53	they serve different backgrounds.
54	
55	## Bearing on the canvas choice
56	
57	The two decisions are coupled, so it is worth taking them together:
58	
59	- Keeping the 2 px outline argues for **32 x 32 or larger**, so that interior area
60	  remains for role differentiation between the scout and the medic.
61	- Dropping the outline makes a **smaller canvas** viable, because the full canvas is
62	  available to the figure — but then the shoulder bar, base bar and solid stalks that the
63	  navy currently carries have to be re-authored as a second teal value or a cream accent,
64	  or the characters lose those landmarks entirely.

37	- **Official PixelLab:** use the parent host's configured connection and inspect
38	  the current tool declarations. The [HTTP connection templates](../../../config/pixellab.codex.http.example.toml)
39	  and [Claude template](../../../config/pixellab.claude.http.example.json) are
40	  inactive examples. Local MCP setup does not create that connection. Preserve
41	  existing parent configuration rather than copying isolated-evaluation flags
42	  that exclude its servers.
43	
44	## Read the setup report
45	
46	The bootstrap command uses only the standard library, so it can report missing
47	runtime dependencies before ordinary local operations are available. With the
48	selected Python, run either the installed package or the copied runner:
49	
50	```text
51	python -m pixl readiness --root CONSUMER --host codex --installation KIT
52	python ABSOLUTE_KIT/scripts/pixl.py readiness --root CONSUMER --host claude --installation ABSOLUTE_KIT
53	```
54	
55	Use actual paths, quoting those containing spaces. `--host` and `--installation`
56	are optional when the available local context is sufficient; supplying them
57	makes the intended installation and host explicit. The command reads inputs and
58	resolves a relative installation path from the consumer root, never the server's
59	working directory. An absolute installation path can point outside the consumer.
60	It returns JSON without publishing project state. When local MCP is already loaded,
61	`pixl_readiness` exposes the same report; discover its exact argument schema.
62	The existing `ready`/`pixl_ready` operation still means production-state readiness.
63	
64	Exit 0 means the local runtime requirements are satisfied, exit 1 means they are
65	incomplete, and exit 2 means invalid input. A zero exit is not proof of named-role
66	loading, official-tool access or authentication. Read each report group; the
67	top-level `status: reported` describes a report, not overall production readiness.
68	
69	The report separates project/installation checks, dependency presence, specialist
70	observations, local operations and official tool visibility. File presence is a
71	static fact. Native role declarations, invocation/completion and successful local
72	tool calls are separate host observations. The runtime does not launch a child,
73	discover remote servers, test authentication, submit generation or infer artistic
74	acceptance. Authentication remains unverified by this report.
75	`specialist.instruction_loading` likewise stays `not_verified`; a caller's
76	availability observation is not an instruction-loading trace.
77	
78	## Supply only observed host facts
79	
80	If the caller has actual session observations, save a small JSON file inside the
81	consumer and pass its project-relative path with `--observations`. Its closed
82	envelope requires `host` (`codex` or `claude`) and an ISO timestamp with timezone
83	in `observed_at`. Optional fields are:
84	
85	- `host_version`: the numeric version string reported by the executable.
86	- `named_role`: `available`, `unavailable` or `not_observed` in that invocation.
87	- `local_tools`: `{names: [...], complete_inventory: boolean}` using bare
88	  `pixl_*` operation names.
89	- `official_tools`: the same shape, using bare official names such as
90	  `pixelart_workbench`.
91	
92	Record the actual observation time and version. Keep native identities, returned
93	files and invocation evidence in the caller's report; `named_role: available`
94	alone does not claim that the specialist completed work. Do not include raw host
95	configuration, credential values, authorization headers or environment dumps.
96	These supplied observations remain explicitly caller-supplied; the runtime does
97	not certify them as direct host discovery.
98	
99	Missing observations remain unobserved. A tool absent from a partial inventory
100	is not known missing. Absence from a caller-supplied complete inventory means
101	only that it was not listed in that capture. A dated `pixl_capabilities` catalog
102	is documentation, not live official-tool visibility.
103	
104	For useful local proof, read a known consumer source with `pixl_source` using its
105	exact file hash and retrieve installed library sources with `pixl_sources`.
106	Those successful calls establish the selected project root and installed
107	resources; a tool list alone does not. Preserve the source bytes and distinguish
108	these local observations from the official provider connection.
109	
110	Return the observed root/installation, available evidence, specific missing setup
111	and next useful action. If official tools were not configured in an isolated
112	invocation, say that; do not invent an authentication failure or service outage.
113	Then follow [everyday production](everyday.md) under the caller's existing scope.
114

2	
3	This is evidence preparation, not a semantic consistency or art-acceptance verdict.

13	
14	def source_evidence(root, source, expected, budget=16384):
15	    """Resolve explicit lines or legacy numbered prose against this file only."""
16	    local = graph.confined(root, source["path"])
17	    result = {
18	        "path": source["path"],
19	        "sha256": expected,
20	        "locator": source.get("locator"),
21	        "absolute_path": str(local),
22	    }

26	        return {**result, "status": "too_large"}
27	    data = local.read_bytes()
28	    actual = sha256(data).hexdigest()
29	    result.update(observed_sha256=actual)
30	    if actual != expected:
31	        return {**result, "status": "changed"}
32	    try:
33	        lines = data.decode("utf-8-sig").splitlines(keepends=True)
34	    except UnicodeError:
35	        return {
36	            **result,
37	            "status": "visual_source",
38	            "instruction": "Inspect the actual referenced artifact through the host.",
39	        }
40	    result["line_count"] = len(lines)
41	    explicit = source.get("lines")
42	    if explicit is not None:
43	        if (
44	            not isinstance(explicit, list)
45	            or len(explicit) != 2

48	            return {
49	                **result,
50	                "status": "invalid_locator",
51	                "reason": "lines must be [first, last] integer bounds",
52	            }
53	        ranges = [explicit]
54	    else:
55	        ranges = [
56	            [int(a), int(b or a)]
57	            for a, b in re.findall(
58	                r"\blines?\s+(\d+)(?:\s*[-–]\s*(\d+))?",

60	                re.IGNORECASE,
61	            )
62	        ]

64	        return {
65	            **result,
66	            "status": "unresolved_locator",
67	            "instruction": "Use file-local lines [first,last] or inspect the named source location; no locator is assumed verified.",
68	        }

70	        return {
71	            **result,
72	            "status": "invalid_locator",
73	            "requested_lines": ranges,
74	            "reason": f"Source has {len(lines)} lines; one or more bounds are outside it.",
75	        }

77	        {"lines": [start, end], "text": "".join(lines[start - 1 : end])}
78	        for start, end in ranges
79	    ]

82	    return {
83	        **result,
84	        "status": "resolved",
85	        "excerpts": excerpts,

87	    }

90	def report(root, packet_path, asset_id=None, path="plar.txt", plan=None, job=None, comparison=None, view="complete", against_plan=None):
91	    if view not in ("complete", "changes"):
92	        raise graph.PixlError("request_review", "view must be complete or changes")
93	    if view == "changes":
94	        if plan is None or against_plan is None:
95	            raise graph.PixlError("request_review", "changes view requires plan and against_plan")
96	        from . import successor_review
97	
98	        return successor_review.report(root, packet_path, plan, against_plan, job, comparison)
99	    if against_plan is not None:
100	        raise graph.PixlError("request_review", "against_plan requires changes view")
101	    if plan is not None:
102	        from . import production_review
103	
104	        return production_review.report(root, packet_path, plan, job, comparison)
105	    if job is not None or comparison is not None:
106	        raise graph.PixlError("request_review", "job/comparison require a connected plan")
107	    from jsonschema import Draft202012Validator
108	
109	    from .plar_prepare import SCHEMA, _artifact, _json_file, _require
110	
111	    root = Path(root).resolve()
112	    packet, digest, packet_path = _json_file(root, packet_path)
113	    _require(
114	        type(packet.get("version")) is int and packet["version"] == 1,
115	        "expected request-review version 1",
116	    )
117	    _require(isinstance(packet.get("sources"), list), "packet sources must be a list")
118	    sources: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
119	    for source in packet["sources"]:
120	        _require(
121	            isinstance(source, dict) and {"path", "sha256", "role"} <= source.keys(),
122	            "packet sources need path, sha256 and role",
123	        )
124	        name = graph.confined(root, source["path"]).relative_to(root).as_posix()
125	        _require(
126	            name not in sources or sources[name]["sha256"] == source["sha256"],
127	            "conflicting source identities",
128	        )
129	        sources[name] = source
130	    pointer = packet.get("request")
131	    _require(
132	        isinstance(pointer, dict) and pointer.get("kind") == "provider_arguments",
133	        "review expects exact provider arguments, not a creative brief",
134	    )
135	    request, request_hash, request_path = _artifact(root, packet.get("request"))
136	    connection = None
137	    if "connection" in pointer:
138	        value, connection_hash, connection_path = _artifact(root, pointer["connection"])
139	        connection = {
140	            "path": connection_path,
141	            "sha256": connection_hash,
142	            "provider": value.get("provider"),
143	            "discovery": value.get("discovery"),
144	            "authorization": value.get("authorization"),
145	        }
146	
147	    plan, plan_hash, plan_path = _artifact(root, packet.get("criteria"))
148	    error = next(Draft202012Validator(SCHEMA).iter_errors(plan), None)
149	    _require(error is None, f"candidate plan: {error.message if error else ''}")
150	    evidence, comparisons, diagnostics = [], [], []
151	    if (
152	        connection
153	        and "provider" in pointer
154	        and pointer["provider"] != connection["provider"]
155	    ):
156	        diagnostics.append(
157	            {
158	                "status": "provider_mismatch",
159	                "packet": pointer["provider"],
160	                "connection": connection["provider"],
161	            }
162	        )
163	
164	    source_bindings = []
165	    for source in packet["sources"]:
166	        local = graph.confined(root, source["path"])
167	        name = local.relative_to(root).as_posix()
168	        observed = (
169	            graph.file_hash(local)
170	            if local.is_file() and local.stat().st_size <= 64 * 1024 * 1024
171	            else None
172	        )
173	        status = (
174	            "current"
175	            if observed == source["sha256"]
176	            else "changed"
177	            if observed is not None
178	            else "unavailable"
179	        )
180	        source_bindings.append(
181	            {**source, "observed_sha256": observed, "binding": status}
182	        )
183	        if status != "current":
184	            diagnostics.append({"source": name, "status": status})
185	        pointers = [source] if "locator" in source or "lines" in source else []
186	        locators = source.get("locators", [])
187	        if isinstance(locators, list) and all(
188	            isinstance(value, str) for value in locators
189	        ):
190	            pointers.extend({**source, "locator": value} for value in locators)
191	        else:
192	            diagnostics.append(
193	                {"packet_source": name, "status": "unresolved_locator_format"}
194	            )
195	        for citation in pointers:
196	            item = source_evidence(root, citation, source["sha256"])
197	            if item not in evidence:

199	            source_bindings[-1].setdefault("source_evidence", []).append(
200	                evidence.index(item)
201	            )
202	            if item["status"] != "resolved":
203	                diagnostics.append(
204	                    {
205	                        "packet_source": name,
206	                        "locator": citation.get("locator"),
207	                        "status": item["status"],
208	                    }
209	                )
210	
211	    for output in plan["outputs"]:

213	            indices = []
214	            for source in criterion["sources"]:
215	                name = graph.confined(root, source["path"]).relative_to(root).as_posix()
216	                _require(
217	                    name in sources, f"criterion source absent from packet: {name}"
218	                )

223	                indices.append(index)

227	                            "output": output["id"],
228	                            "criterion": criterion["id"],
229	                            "source": index,

232	                    )

248	            }

57	old acceptance does not close it. Existing unsupported or unavailable observations

95	[MCP tool overview](https://api.pixellab.ai/mcp/docs), and the actual connected

115	Keep those observations separate from the mechanical measurements. For a matching
116	queue consumer, [isolated consumer execution](consumer-execution.md) runs the

118	coverage without changing production state.
119

121	observation JSON: reviewer, actual observation time, evidence files, explicit
122	criterion judgments and `action` (`record`, `nominate` or `complete`). It derives
123	evidence bindings and preserves failures and superseded verdicts. Supply the
124	context's `binding_hash` inside the observation and its current `state_hash` as
125	`expect`. Missing viewing produces an unavailable judgment, not a pass. Prepared
126	inspection packets retain their [own view-coverage workflow](inspection.md).
127	
128	After an interrupted review, reload current state and repeat the same review ID
129	and observation to finish recovery. Changing the observation requires a new review
130	ID and explicit supersession. An already accepted review can be retried without
131	new publication; this does not establish a new observation.
132	
133	## 6. Review the family, integrate and return usable files
134	
135	Use `family` for exact baseline/member/destination context. `family-snapshot`
136	retains the selected package as a candidate; its creation-time `accepted:false`
137	does not describe later acceptance. Review its actual collective appearance and
138	destination through the same `review-context` and `candidate-review` operations.
139	Nominate/complete only after the applicable criteria pass. Follow
140	[family delivery](family-delivery.md) for member selection and integration.
141	
142	Reread the selected queue before returning. Save the expert summary, useful file
143	locators, provenance, findings, limits and caller actions through `plar handoff` /
144	`pixl_plar_handoff`. Choose CLI `--view caller` or MCP `view: "caller"` for the
145	[compact caller result](../../../resources/spec/caller-result.md); omitting it
146	keeps the existing receipt. Put the bounded ordinary summary in `details.caller`,
147	and retain the full observations in other details fields and referenced reports. Its two inputs come from the same fresh focused PLAR read:
148	`requirements_hash` and `production.continuation.state_hash` for `expect`.
149	The queue's top-level `hash` is only for queue saves. Return the caller view with
150	its exact handoff locator, actual deliverables and remaining decisions. Assignment
151	status and integration findings remain your claims; current production facts and
152	the immediate next action come from the runtime. Detailed checks remain exactly
153	retrievable, and a referenced resume must be read in full before acting.
154	The next agent rereads current state rather than blindly executing an old snapshot.
155	
156	The stop condition is the assignment's useful delivered outcome or a precise
157	remaining dependency with preserved work. A valid request, journal or package
158	alone does not establish visual quality or destination acceptance.

authorization and unfinished attempts.

## 1. Locate the assignment and select its asset

Read the caller's brief, actual consumers/backend states and available reference
images. Use [PLAR](../../plar/SKILL.md) to allocate missing/reusable assets when that
inventory is needed. If a queue already exists, use the path the caller selected:
different queue files can retain different generations of the same asset.

`queue.working`. Its older `plar.txt` remains historical production context. In
another project substitute its actual queue and asset; these names and its 16px
cells are not universal requirements.

From the consumer directory, select its Python and the complete installed plugin:

```powershell
$Project = (Resolve-Path ".").Path
$Python = "C:/path/to/selected/python.exe"
$Runner = "C:/path/to/installed/pixl/scripts/pixl.py"

$Queue = "authoring-plar.txt"
$Asset = "queue.working"
$Selected = pixl plar read --path $Queue --asset $Asset --root $Project | ConvertFrom-Json
```

the corresponding read is `pixl_plar_read` with

## 2. Resume the actual production step

and `production.continuation`. If there is no production link, continue at step 3.

```powershell

$StoreFolder = Join-Path $Project $Store
```

remain visible. Use the [provider recovery procedure](provider-recovery.md) for
uncertain submission or retrieval, and [source retention](library-retention.md)
when a package update exposes missing old source bytes.

## 3. Make the first request or extend the family

For one selected asset, [PLAR preparation](../../plar/references/prepare.md) takes
ordinary JSON: sourced candidate controls, exact review criteria and a provider
request. The caller compares the literal packet against the original brief,
references and code through [request-review](request-review.md). Keep measured
facts, caller decisions and expert design proposals distinct. Carry useful pixel

For an adopted baseline and related stages, use the [connected plan contract](../../../resources/spec/production-plan.md):
`production-plan` saves the reviewed stages and `stage-prepare` binds the exact


## 4. Generate through official PixelLab

new publication; this does not establish a new observation.

does not describe later acceptance. Review its actual collective appearance and

[family delivery](family-delivery.md) for member selection and integration.

`requirements_hash` and `production.continuation.state_hash` for `expect`.
The queue's top-level `hash` is only for queue saves. Return the caller view with
its exact handoff locator, actual deliverables and remaining decisions. Assignment
status and integration findings remain your claims; current production facts and
the immediate next action come from the runtime. Detailed checks remain exactly

1	# Everyday asset production
2	
3	Use this path for an assigned asset or family. PIXL supplies visual expertise through
4	the host model; the caller supplies the assignment and project authority. The local
5	runtime preserves requirements, attempts and reviews. Official PixelLab tools do
6	the generation. Start at the project's current step, keeping its existing choices,
7	authorization and unfinished attempts.
8	
9	## 1. Locate the assignment and select its asset
10	
11	Read the caller's brief, actual consumers/backend states and available reference
12	images. Use [PLAR](../../plar/SKILL.md) to allocate missing/reusable assets when that
13	inventory is needed. If a queue already exists, use the path the caller selected:
14	different queue files can retain different generations of the same asset.
15	
16	This running example is the existing queue successor: `authoring-plar.txt`, asset
17	`queue.working`. Its older `plar.txt` remains historical production context. In
18	another project substitute its actual queue and asset; these names and its 16px
19	cells are not universal requirements.
20	
21	From the consumer directory, select its Python and the complete installed plugin:
22	
23	```powershell
24	$Project = (Resolve-Path ".").Path
25	$Python = "C:/path/to/selected/python.exe"
26	$Runner = "C:/path/to/installed/pixl/scripts/pixl.py"
27	function pixl { & $Python $Runner @args }
28	$Queue = "authoring-plar.txt"
29	$Asset = "queue.working"
30	$Selected = pixl plar read --path $Queue --asset $Asset --root $Project | ConvertFrom-Json
31	```
32	
33	Set the two executable paths to the installation in use. Neither is relative to
34	the production store. For local MCP, the server's configured root is `$Project`;
35	the corresponding read is `pixl_plar_read` with
36	`{"path":"authoring-plar.txt","asset_id":"queue.working"}`.
37	See [identities and paths](identities-and-paths.md) for exact root and hash rules.
38	
39	## 2. Resume the actual production step
40	
41	Read selected requirements, source changes, reference roles, unresolved questions
42	and `production.continuation`. If there is no production link, continue at step 3.
43	Otherwise derive the store from that continuation, not from the asset's name:
44	
45	```powershell
46	$Store = $Selected.production.continuation.store
47	$StoreFolder = Join-Path $Project $Store
48	$State = "$Store/state.px"
49	$StateFile = Join-Path $Project $State
50	pixl workflow $StateFile --root $Project
51	pixl jobs $StateFile --root $Project
52	```
53	
54	Follow current pending/unknown job observations before another submission. A
55	delivered continuation means consume the accepted result unless a new requirement
56	actually calls for revision. A new requirement must have an explicit successor;
57	old acceptance does not close it. Existing unsupported or unavailable observations
58	remain visible. Use the [provider recovery procedure](provider-recovery.md) for
59	uncertain submission or retrieval, and [source retention](library-retention.md)
60	when a package update exposes missing old source bytes.
61	
62	## 3. Make the first request or extend the family
63	
64	For one selected asset, [PLAR preparation](../../plar/references/prepare.md) takes
65	ordinary JSON: sourced candidate controls, exact review criteria and a provider
66	request. The caller compares the literal packet against the original brief,
67	references and code through [request-review](request-review.md). Keep measured
68	facts, caller decisions and expert design proposals distinct. Carry useful pixel
69	art judgment into prompts and criteria without turning sample recipes into owner
70	requirements.
71	
72	For an adopted baseline and related stages, use the [connected plan contract](../../../resources/spec/production-plan.md):
73	`production-plan` saves the reviewed stages and `stage-prepare` binds the exact
74	accepted upstream inputs to a request. These public operations construct the
75	records. For a delivery composed of accepted existing outputs, a plan with
76	`stages: []` binds those outputs without creating a generation stage. Reuse
77	accepted existing art when it satisfies the assigned successor;
78	do not mislabel reused bytes as generated under that successor.
79	
80	For this retained successor, orientation is:
81	
82	```powershell
83	pixl context $StateFile provenance-correction.plan --view authoring --root $Project --result-path work/current-authoring.json
84	pixl request-review $State --plan provenance-correction.plan --against-plan authoring-01.plan --view changes --root $Project --result-path work/current-changes.json
85	```
86	
87	Use fresh output names. Follow indexed intake when applicable and both full-report
88	retrievals for literal comparison; the concise view cannot decide consistency.
89	For another project use plan IDs from its saved context. This explicit pair need
90	not be directly consecutive.
91	
92	## 4. Generate through official PixelLab
93	
94	Use the current [official platform docs](https://www.pixellab.ai/docs),
95	[MCP tool overview](https://api.pixellab.ai/mcp/docs), and the actual connected
96	declaration for the operation. Match reference roles to supported image inputs or
97	handles; a local filename in prose does not supply its pixels. The host makes the
98	paid official call under the assignment's established scope and authorization.
99	See [operation selection](pixellab-operations.md) for capability-specific choices.
100	
101	The local sequence is `job-prepare` (or the preparation from step 3), then
102	`job-dispatch`. Dispatch returns the exact call for the host and claims this attempt.
103	Use the observed provider result with `job-observe`; use the provider's actual
104	status/retrieval tool until the result is available. Download actual returned bytes
105	and use `job-import` for the saved output. Refresh the canonical state hash before
106	each publication. The [provider procedure](provider-recovery.md) defines arguments
107	and unknown-outcome recovery; a local claim or elapsed time is not remote success.
108	
109	## 5. Review the candidate and complete its task
110	
111	Read `review-context` / `pixl_review_context` for the exact candidate, current
112	criteria, binding hash and canonical state hash. Inspect the real file at native
113	and appropriate enlarged scales, measure its applicable constraints, and exercise
114	its actual consumer. Animation needs temporal viewing; tiles need neighborhoods.
115	Keep those observations separate from the mechanical measurements. For a matching
116	queue consumer, [isolated consumer execution](consumer-execution.md) runs the
117	shipped capture/check/import path and retains actual motion and preference-switch
118	coverage without changing production state.
119	
120	Use [candidate-review](../../../resources/spec/candidate-review.md) with an ordinary
121	observation JSON: reviewer, actual observation time, evidence files, explicit
122	criterion judgments and `action` (`record`, `nominate` or `complete`). It derives
123	evidence bindings and preserves failures and superseded verdicts. Supply the
124	context's `binding_hash` inside the observation and its current `state_hash` as
125	`expect`. Missing viewing produces an unavailable judgment, not a pass. Prepared
126	inspection packets retain their [own view-coverage workflow](inspection.md).
127	
128	After an interrupted review, reload current state and repeat the same review ID
129	and observation to finish recovery. Changing the observation requires a new review
130	ID and explicit supersession. An already accepted review can be retried without
131	new publication; this does not establish a new observation.
132	
133	## 6. Review the family, integrate and return usable files
134	
135	Use `family` for exact baseline/member/destination context. `family-snapshot`
136	retains the selected package as a candidate; its creation-time `accepted:false`
137	does not describe later acceptance. Review its actual collective appearance and
138	destination through the same `review-context` and `candidate-review` operations.
139	Nominate/complete only after the applicable criteria pass. Follow
140	[family delivery](family-delivery.md) for member selection and integration.
141	
142	Reread the selected queue before returning. Save the expert summary, useful file
143	locators, provenance, findings, limits and caller actions through `plar handoff` /
144	`pixl_plar_handoff`. Choose CLI `--view caller` or MCP `view: "caller"` for the
145	[compact caller result](../../../resources/spec/caller-result.md); omitting it
146	keeps the existing receipt. Put the bounded ordinary summary in `details.caller`,
147	and retain the full observations in other details fields and referenced reports. Its two inputs come from the same fresh focused PLAR read:
148	`requirements_hash` and `production.continuation.state_hash` for `expect`.
149	The queue's top-level `hash` is only for queue saves. Return the caller view with
150	its exact handoff locator, actual deliverables and remaining decisions. Assignment
151	status and integration findings remain your claims; current production facts and
152	the immediate next action come from the runtime. Detailed checks remain exactly
153	retrievable, and a referenced resume must be read in full before acting.
154	The next agent rereads current state rather than blindly executing an old snapshot.
155	
156	The stop condition is the assignment's useful delivered outcome or a precise
157	remaining dependency with preserved work. A valid request, journal or package
158	alone does not establish visual quality or destination acceptance.
